title: A Post-Implementation Performance Prediction Method with HLS Optimization Directives
problem: High-Level Synthesis (HLS) performance prediction methods fail to capture complex directive-hardware interactions and resource reuse issues, leading to inaccurate timing and power predictions for directive-optimized circuits.
motivation: Accurate post-implementation performance prediction reduces HLS design iteration time and enables designers to make optimization trade-offs without costly re-synthesis cycles.
method: The method converts the circuit into a graph that includes HLS directives (optimization instructions) and resource reuse information. A Graph Neural Network model—using TransformerConv layers and pooling—learns from this graph to spot timing delays. It then predicts the circuit's critical path delay (how fast it runs), power consumption, and resource utilization.
key_novelty: The method predicts post-implementation circuit performance by incorporating resource reuse patterns from HLS directives into the graph representation, which prior approaches didn't do.
contributions: Graph Builder that integrates HLS optimization directives and resource reuse into the graph representation
TransformerConv-based GNN with aggregation pooling for performance feature extraction
Achieves 3.87–8.08% prediction error on critical path, power, and resource utilization
Demonstrates strong generalization to unseen kernels

metrics.accuracy: 3.87–8.08% error on critical path delay, power, resource utilization

baselines: state-of-the-art HLS performance prediction methods (unspecified names)
limitations: Evaluation limited to HLS C/C++ kernels; applicability to other synthesis domains not discussed.
